chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya and al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The menstruating woman in ihram wears a khallaqah (garment) under her clothes." And there is no objection to her wearing trousers at all times; this was narrated.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَةُ: The female in the state of Ihram (consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: At all times / in any condition
key_terms.غِلاَلَةً: A specific type of garment (khallaqah), typically a sleeveless upper garment

ai.seo_question: What clothing is a menstruating woman allowed to wear while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical application of the general prohibition on women wearing veils (*qubbur*) and head coverings (*khimar*) during ihram by specifying that a menstruating woman may wear a *ghilalah* (a loose upper garment) beneath her outer layers to maintain modesty without violating the ihram restrictions. The explicit permission to wear *sarawil* (trousers) at all times highlights the juristic distinction between the upper body, where the veil is restricted, and the lower body, which remains flexible, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*rukhas*) for women during their natural physiological states.
